title: Sprint closeout 1:1 prep — Jia -> report
summary: Prep notes for a focused 25-minute sprint-closeout 1:1. Goal: align on priorities, unblock ramping work, and set growth micro-goals for next sprint.
content:
Meeting logistics
- Length: 25 min (quick + actionable) — start on time, leave 5m for action-item confirmation.
- Date/time: 2026-09-20 10:00am PT.
- Location: Zoom / @jia-zhang-1on1 Slack reminder.

Agenda (top priorities, timeboxed)
1) Quick wins & metrics (5m) — show delta vs last 2 sprints
   - Throughput: infra e2e job latency median down 8% (see PR 317 perf numbers).
   - Error budget burn: 0.3% last sprint (on target).
   - Personal note: celebrate the load-test harness improvement — call it out explicitly.

2) Blockers & escalation (7m)
   - PLAT-1423: flaky cache invalidation on multi-tenant tests — current status: reproducer added, but still timing-dependent.
     - Draft troubleshooting plan: add deterministic seed to test harness; add extra logs around kv-cache eviction.
     - Risk: if not fixed before next deploy, can cause rollback on heavy canary.
   - Question to unblock: do you need an extra pair on the reproducer? (Offer: loop in Ravi for an afternoon pairing).

3) Roadmap alignment & trade-offs (6m)
   - Can we deprioritize non-critical batching telemetry for next sprint to free up 1 engineer-day? Pros: frees bandwidth for reproducer. Cons: delays long-tail observability.
   - Ask for the report's recommendation and reasoning; push for a short decision rubric (impact x cost quick check).

4) Career / coaching micro-goal (5m)
   - Focus suggestion for next sprint: shipping one end-to-end ownership item (reproducer -> fix -> small canary) and publishing a short runbook.
   - Skill focus: move from debugging to system-level mitigation design (doc the fallback strategy, trade-offs).
   - Offer: I'll pair-review proposed runbook and help craft a fragment for team onboarding doc.

5) Confirm actions & next steps (2m)

Notes to self (manager perspective)
- Tone: pragmatic, enabling — avoid micromanaging details of reproducer, instead emphasize shipping a small end-to-end outcome.
- Keep recognition specific: cite PR #317 and call out "made load-test stable enough to benchmark".
- Be explicit about timelines: aim for reproducer PR by Wed EOD; if not, escalate to SRE rotation.
- Watch for signs of burnout — report has worked overtime last 3 days (check in empathetically).

Draft scripts / questions to surface during 1:1
- "What's the one smallest change that would make you unblock this week?"
- "If you had one extra engineer for half a sprint, where would you put them?"
- "What are you learning from this flake — is there an opportunity to generalize the fix?"

Quick metrics snapshot to request live during meeting
- Link to perf dashboard: ask for median p50/p95 for the e2e job and error-rate by region.
- Tests: failing count over last 48h for PLAT-1423 test group.

Action items (tentative, to confirm in meeting)
- [Report] Add deterministic seed and extra logs to reproducer test (owner: report; due: 2026-09-22).
- [Jia] File a short escalation note to SRE rotation if reproducer not merged by Wed EOD (owner: Jia; due: 2026-09-23).
- [Report + Ravi] Pair for 3 hours on Thursday afternoon to accelerate repro/fix (owner: Report/Ravi; due: 2026-09-24).
- [Report] Draft 1-page runbook for the flaky eviction scenario, include rollback/fallback steps (owner: report; due: 2026-09-28).
- [Jia] Review runbook and add to team onboarding snippets (owner: Jia; due: 2026-09-30).

Follow-up and observability
- Suggest adding a short telemetry flag that emits when eviction happens under canary traffic — low-cost signal to avoid surprise rollbacks.
- If runbook exists, map it to alert playbook and link to SLO runbook.

Open questions (to resolve during sync)
- Is the flaky behavior limited to specific hardware/region? (If yes, we can route traffic away temporarily.)
- Can we amortize additional testing infra costs from the Optimize budget? Who signs off?

Scratch / quick thoughts (private)
- Consider a "canary-only" feature flag to constrain risk and speed up testing. Noted: requires CI gating updates.
- Long-term: author a short postmortem template for recurring flake classes.

References I want them to pull in live
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/317 (perf + test changes)
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PLAT-1423
- Confluence retro: https://confluence.redwood/sprint-42-retro

Meeting follow-up template (to send immediately after meeting)
- Short summary (2 sentences)
- Confirmed action items with owners + due dates
- Any escalations + next check-in time
- Call out a single appreciation line for concrete work shipped

Personal reminder to self after meeting
- Block 30m on Friday to check progress on reproducer and triage CI signals.
- If reproducer stalls, schedule a quick ad-hoc with SRE and Platform leads.

Todo (manager admin)
- Add follow-up Slack thread to #platform-ops and pin the runbook when done.
- Move final runbook into the team onboarding folder in Confluence.

End of doc — keep this as scratchpad for the 1:1. Will convert confirmed action items to calendar invites and update Jira tickets post-call.
